english: The only not-disintegrated thing in the central chamber is this stone slab.
It's just very, very cooked.
A table. It was once a stone table. Now it is as scorched as the rest of the tea shop.
Move this thing. It is surely hiding something important.
Maybe... leave it alone. Your arms cannot carry that burden.
Ah. Yes, a table. It must have been flipped over by the force of the explosion.
Beneath.
Everything is horrific beneath.
It could cover something. But moving it alone would be difficult.
It could cover something. Make sure the goblin helps out.
Leave this for last. If you are able.
So whisper the Strings in your ears.
Hm? You want to flip the table?
It's damn heavy, but... maybe we can do it together.
Once you've flipped tables, you shall be TRUE brothers.
Try to move the stone table.
E-Later.
You make your best attempt, but the big block of scorched wood just won't move.
Damn, the goblin says, panting. "Heavy."
Let's... look around more. Come back to this later, I guess.
Doing this alone is nearly impossible. If only you had a companion of some kind...
You can do this. Alone. Right?
You can do this. Alone. Maybe.
Of course you can!
The world quakes at your feet. It moves at your touch!
FLIP. THAT. TABLE!
Alone, it would be difficult.
Perhaps you should find assistance.
There is something interesting here.
However, make sure you look around first.
Then do not bother. It is just a table.
You grab the thick table with your gloved hands.
Gripping it firmly. Strongly.
Snell copies your movements.
On three.
One. Two.
Three!
(Flip the table.)
You stare into the dark corner of the tea shop.
Midst soot and broken tiles, you see a corpse.
Of circumstance. Of whispers-in-the-pipes.
Of a son in search of his father - SHE PAID.
It almost disappears into the destruction around it.
An aura of sorrow. This is pure tragedy, beyond any imaginable degree.
It's a...
Snell stares at it. He is silent.
Give him a second. He'll appreciate it.
One casualty. Report it.
Gods be good...
Huh.
Yeah, this is... a bit out of your pay grade.
(Lower your head in respect.)
(Whisper to yourself.) "Urth Be Blessed."
He flinches and looks at you.
Mm. Yeah. Confirmed.
You spend a moment alone in silence.
You spend a moment next to Snell in silence.
Your thoughts landing on the disfigured remains.
It haunts you.
Your words reach no one.
Snell nods slowly.
Your words hang in the air. No one responds.
Yet it is a comfort nonetheless.
The corpse appears completely charred to you. Such destruction would make it very difficult to identify.
The corpse appears completely charred to you.
The size is average. In human terms. Somewhat slender.
The size is average. You think.
Hard to make out anything other than a silhouette.
She did not deserve this end.
You take a few careful steps up to... it.
Then you kneel down.
Most of the creature is burnt beyond recognition.
So there's only two key areas to focus on.
The hands or the head. Choose.
There's a dirty joke here somewhere.
Not the time, nor the place.
Be respectful.
The goblin steels himself.
How much experience do you have with... corpses, Cleric?
Your thoughts land on anatomy books. Basic medicine training. Nothing practical.
You're an expert.
In your field.
Death.
You know it. You fear it.
You were far too young.
(Clear your throat.)
The goblin breaks his intense stare-down at the corpse and turns to you.
He is afraid the corpse will awaken.
Not an unreasonable concern.
Cleric.
Experience with corpses? None.
I am Urthguard. Not Health Services.
I can handle it.
Not much. What about you?
Great. Guess we'll do this one step at a time.
Guess that's fine. Revivify probably stopped working here a while ago.
Good to hear.
I'm no expert. But you know... part of the gig.
Yeah, right. Like those dainty little claws have ever touched a corpse.
A lie. He wants to seem more experienced than he is.
We should do a preliminary checkup. Just to scope out the scene.
Then we'll get a transport to the... Lichhouse, I guess.
Luckily it's close by.
We should have Visken examine it.
A preliminary checkup, huh?
Uh-huh.
He is barely listening to you.
I'll check the head. You, uh...
Check the hands. Or something.
He is keeping a healthy distance. The goblin is afraid.
He does not want to touch the corpse. You feel bad for him.
You are not afraid.
Approach it. Do your job.
Nasty business this turned into.
Well. Time to go to work.
(Step up.)
You take a few careful steps up to... it.
(Kneel down.)
Seeing it up close causes you to shake.
Your flesh feels the flames.
You share the bond of death.
(Look at the torso.)
(Focus on the hands.)
A dark mass. Once skin.
Now appears to be but a solid mass.
It does not even smell.
She was incinerated. Fully. In an instant.
The intense heat caused rapid muscle contraction, freezing the woman in place.
She placed herself in this position. Most likely to take cover from the explosion.
The heat must have been the source of death. A quick death.
Nothing but blackened, brittle carbon residue.
However, you are quite certain this was a woman.
The mortician will have to determine that.
Whatever led her to this corner, it was quick.
(Just look at something else.)
Got it. Good info.
Snell approaches, just a few steps.
He leans in, slightly closer.
Too far to see anything.
The poor goblin.
You see the left hand is half-destroyed.
Perhaps they landed on it.
Could have shattered in the fall, if the source of the fire was instantaneous enough.
But most likely, the fire would've taken at least half a minute to be lethal.
And only if the fire source was hot enough to cook the target's brain.
The thought causes your stomach to churn.
The right hand is clenched near the victim's hip.
Holding something.
A clue! Of course.
You've read stories like this. The victim always grips something important when they die.
Looks like something brittle in the grip. Perhaps leave it for later.
You'd have to have a real gentle touch not to break the content of that fist.
Go for it!
No. This is a bad idea unless you want to break that fist in a thousand pieces.
But hey. Maybe you do.
Pry the hand open, carefully...
(Leave it for later.)
Slowly and deliberately you sneak your fingers underneath the fingers.
And something comes loose.
A chain.
A thin gold chain, or parts of it.
Interesting.
You attempt to pry and dig, but clearly you're not doing it very well.
Because soon enough the charred hand crackles and the corpse soot...
Oh, gods save us all.
Your everything shivers.
There's CORPSE STUFF all over your HANDS!
I don't like this. I don't like this. I don't like this.
(Muffle a scream.)
In your panic, the hand disintegrated further, creating a pile of dust and chunks on the scorched floor.
You take a deep breath.
Your gloves. They are covered. In PERSON.
It is horrific to be so close to death.
A person stops being a person when their soul leaves. It's okay.
As the terror wears off, and the soot comes off, you find something in the mess you made.
Glimmering.
However, the second after you see it, you watch it begin to GLOW.
An esoteric glow.
Then it starts to break apart in front of your eyes.
The gold chain, within seconds, turning into another pile of dust.
The fuck?
That was... magic, right?
A cursed necklace?
To you, maybe.
The goblin grimaces.
Perhaps a delayed reaction?
A defense mechanism.
Nothing you can deal with now.
Boring.
For the best. Yeah.
The mortician will handle it.
I, uh...
Not much to see. Fire's burned off... everything.
No pain. This was an instant destruction of mind and soul. You sense it by looking at this twisted husk of a person.
It was a quick death. Gods be good.
The thought of one moment being HERE - another being NOT - causes your stomach to churn.
While charred beyond recognition, the skull itself is fairly intact.
The mouth is intact. Good.
So you can have someone to talk to, of course.
Speak with Dead. It requires an intact mouth on the corpse to successfully mimic speech.
Even in this condition, the corpse should be a valid target.
Do I notice anything else?
A good question.
Looking for distinguishing features, you do notice something interesting.
The ears.
Ears?
Yes.
I've seen ears before.
(Look at them. Closely.)
Look closer.
He squints.
Barely there. What about them?
Look closer.
Is the shape off to you?
Sure. What am I supposed to...?
Well, yeah. Because of the fire. Unless you mean...
He tilts his head. "Oh."
Oh.
Wait, wait, wait.
Despite barely keeping a recognizable form, what remains of the ears have a peculiar shape.
They're sharp. Pointy.
They're pointy.
Oh.
He looks around.
There's only one humanoid creature on the coast with this body size and pointy ears.
Not an orc. Not a gnome.
Oh yeah. Orcs and Gnomes have pointy ears too. But... this does indeed not look like one of those.
(Mutter to yourself.) "And not a human..."
The goblin takes a step back. "No. No chance."
Denial. For both of you. It's unbelievable, but...
Oh. Oh boy.
Just the concept of such a rare creature being found in this second-rate tea shop...
There is no doubt.
Of course. Something like...
Gods be good.
Your city is in trouble.
Oh no.
Illym weeps.
Her children are SLAVES to FASCISM.
Your companion glares at the corpse. His head then slowly turns towards you.
Oh no.
Oh dear gods.
It's a...
It's an elf.
It's a damn elf!
Scent of Ukkul 'midst flame a-miss...
This is the death you fear. The dramatic end to your career.
Did they know? No. They couldn't have.
Yet you have, through no means of your own, landed in this trapped hallway of a mission.
You only have one choice now.
Find out exactly why this happened. Who killed the elf? Who blew up the tea shop?
You feel the answer must lie below- far, far below...
If Meriadoc is correct, your goal lies within the Pillar...
Your eyes follow the towering dark knight as he walks past, heading down the stairs.
The body is secured.
Good, good, the pale man answers behind his desk.
Snell leans against the iron slab, his eyes fastened entirely upon the elvish corpse across the chamber.
I think I expected a dwarf.
Huh?
A dwarf.
(Make a manly grunt to acknowledge him.)
What? Why?
The tea shop used to be a gathering place for the Azgals.
My first thought was of in-fighting. Or political assassination.
But an elf...?
There's like three of them. In the entire city.
(Don't say anything for a while.)
What should I say?
After a few seconds, the goblin scoffs and rubs his eyes.
Did the dwarves have a deal with Illym?
Did Drummer?
He lets out a big sigh. "Guess we've got more questions to ask."
Discuss the quest, of course.
Just share your feelings.
Ask him about it. Like, how fucked you both are.
Just speak.
This is a mess.
How bad is this?
Elves are scary.
A right fucking mess.
The Illym are powerful, even in Norvik.
If one of their own got offed...
Yeah. Could spell trouble for sure.
I'm inclined to agree.
Should be easy to identify an elf, right?
I don't like Visken. We shouldn't have brought the elf here. (Whisper, so the pale man doesn't overhear.)
This is above my rank.
M-"So... what now?"
You'd think that. I'm guessing it'll be impossible.
Look, I'll say it again. He's a weirdo.
But the Old Lady has a deal with him.
So for better or worse, he's our guy.
The connection here is interesting. They're both strange entities here in this strange city.
Mm.
But I don't see anyone jumping at the chance, so.
You're still serving the Old Lady. For now.
He's ordering you around again. But...
Perhaps this is not the time to complain.
He takes a deep breath.
The goblin does not look forward to reporting all of this.
Gather any remaining clues in the tea shop.
Then we report to Lady Sageleaf.
He snaps his fingers. "ASAP."
You hear the pale man clear his throat across the circular chamber.
Cleric. I am finished with my report.
However, it is quite late. Please, return in the morning and we shall discuss this.
Then he just walks away, leaving you and your companion alone in the lichhouse.
(Give Visken a thumbs up.)
I want to check out the corpse again.
Ah, yeah. You obviously also want to do the thing.
The thing?
What thing?
(Just stare at him.)
You know. The thing.
He holds up a hand to his mouth and mimics talking.
What is he implying?
Tell him: no thank you.
No thank you. I'll skip.
Elaborate.
What thing?
What?
I'll skip. Whatever it is you're implying.
Fucking hells, Cleric, no!
He groans.
You know. The thing you clerics do? With the corpses?
What's it called, the uh... when you speak with the dead?
You never had a chance to cast Speak with Dead before coming here.
Speak with Dead?
The spell? Speak with Dead?
Yeah. What's it called?
Speak with Dead.
He glares at you.
Are you making fun of me?
No. It's called Speak with Dead.
Right.
He closes his eyes and groans.
Heh. He's embarrassed.
Oh. It's just called that? Right. That's the one.
Right. That is a thing I am... somewhat capable of doing.
We'll see about that.
No way. That's creepy.
I never did any corpse-stuff at the Towers. However, I believe it is time to do so.
He squints. "Phrasing it like that doesn't... doesn't evoke trust in your abilities, Cleric."
I guess we will.
I don't disagree.
Great.
...And don't call it corpse-stuff. Doesn't sound good.
Sounds good to you.
Agreed.
But you get five questions from that spell, right?
With that you should easily be able to figure out who, what, why, when. And so on.
Perhaps Visken can tell you something about that spell...
You already memorized this spell. Go make use of it.
Let's talk to Visken. Hear his report.
Let's talk to Visken in the morning. Hear out his report.
Let me check the corpse again.
Before anything else, we should explain all this to Lady Sageleaf.
In the morning, we should report to Lady Sageleaf right away.
Oh. Wait, but... doesn't it take years to learn that shit?
(Shrug.) "Eh. Give me an afternoon or two."
I think I lost something when I fell into the river. But it's coming back to me.
Well, well. Aren't you just absolutely horrifying.
Sounds... worrying. But good. Just try to get back into the groove quickly, alright?
Yeah. Sure. Lead the way.
Yeah. It's late anyhow.
Oh. Yeah, why not. You lead the way.
Good thinking. Let's go.
Yeah. In the morning. Good idea.
The goblin yawns.
E-Alright. Let's get going.
How exciting.
Not often you get to deal with elves.
This is a terrible idea. You should have run away the second you saw those ears.
The pale man knows what to do. It was smart to let him handle the corpse.
A new quest.
The pale man will know.
This is a real mess, isn't it?
How screwed am I?
I hate elves.
Bringing the corpse to Visken was a mistake. I don't trust that guy.
(Don't say anything. Just stand there like a man without a plan.)
E-Let's go speak with Visken.
(Look over to Visken.)
Perhaps.
Oh yes. You've really fallen into the bog this time.
You will survive.
This will be your end.
They always seem to pop up where they don't belong.
You've never even met an elf.
Now you have. And that elf does not belong.
What other choice did you have?
Eh. He's alright. Just stay on his good side and you'll be fine.
I'm afraid it's quite late at the moment, Cleric.
Come back in the morning. You shall have my report then.
Then he just walks away.
Wow. This fucking guy...
It is late. He needs to sleep.
Heh. Power move.
E-Oh well.
